verdict.rationale: Neon's hosted MCP server exposes a documented 113-tool surface with explicit read-only mode (?readonly=true), category scoping, and project scoping, verified keylessly via the list-tools endpoint returning tools tagged readOnlySafe:true and injecting a guardrail notice that write tools are removed. Runtime probes confirm the server is live, OAuth-gated, and the read-only filtering works as documented, directly matching the story of scoped tools distinguishing read-only from destructive actions. missing for 10: independent third-party (non-Neon) hands-on report of an agent actually being blocked from a destructive action in practice, beyond Neon's own docs/probes.
